documents.title: Generative AI Guidelines for Classroom Use
documents.summary: BU's AI Development Accelerator recommends that faculty state a GenAI policy in the syllabus, explain it in week one, and design process-focused assignments. It cautions against relying on detectors and points faculty to the free TerrierGPT platform. It sets no university-wide rule.
documents.stance_why: The page is a set of 'recommendations' from AIDA leadership; it says 'faculty must proactively guide' use and 'review what constitutes allowable versus misuse ... in their course', leaving the stance to each instructor, so it delegates.

units.why: The opening says faculty 'must proactively guide appropriate and ethical use in coursework', placing the decision and the guidance duty on each instructor, so it is P04 (instructor sets the rule), addressed to instructors, before-course, must.
units.anchor: BU faculty must proactively guide appropriate and ethical use in coursework

units.why: 'It is therefore important for faculty to review what constitutes allowable versus misuse of GenAI in their course' leaves the allowed/misuse line to each course; P04 fits, not P09 since no syllabus statement is mentioned here.
units.anchor: review what constitutes allowable versus misuse of GenAI in their course

units.why: 'State your policy on GenAI use explicitly in the course syllabus' is a recommendation that every syllabus carry an AI statement (P09), addressed to instructors at course start.
units.anchor: State your policy on GenAI use explicitly in the course syllabus

units.why: The syllabus statement 'includes disclosing how the instructors (faculty and student teachers) will use GenAI for lecture preparation, presentations, grading'; this is instructor disclosure of own AI use (P47), not the general syllabus duty.
units.anchor: disclosing how the instructors (faculty and student teachers) will use GenAI

units.why: 'Take time in the first week of class to explain your policy and its rationale' tells instructors to communicate expectations at course start; P09 (communicating AI expectations) fits best.
units.anchor: Take time in the first week of class to explain your policy and its rationale

units.why: 'Make clear distinctions between acceptable and unacceptable uses' asks instructors to make the line explicit to students; communicating expectations, so P09.
units.anchor: Make clear distinctions between acceptable and unacceptable uses

units.why: 'They are responsible for verifying the accuracy of any AI-generated content' states that students must check AI output, which is P31 (verify AI output).
units.anchor: They are responsible for verifying the accuracy of any AI-generated content

units.why: 'Submitting GenAI-generated work as their own original work may constitute plagiarism' classifies passing off AI output as plagiarism, i.e. misconduct (P36).
units.anchor: Submitting GenAI-generated work as their own original work may constitute plagiarism

units.why: 'Misuse of GenAI can lead to violations of the university's academic conduct policies' ties misuse to the integrity process (P36).
units.anchor: Misuse of GenAI can lead to violations of the university’s academic conduct policies

units.why: Faculty are 'encouraged to design assignments that integrate GenAI in a way that enhances learning, such as using it for brainstorming, editing, or reflection'; assignment redesign around AI (P35) that encourages AI use.
units.anchor: Design assignments that integrate GenAI in a way that enhances learning

units.why: 'Emphasize learning goals over performance metrics, which can help reduce misuse' is an assignment and grading design recommendation aimed at AI misuse (P35).
units.anchor: Emphasize learning goals over performance metrics, which can help reduce misuse

units.why: 'Consider process-focused assignments and assessing intermediate milestones' (drafts, revisions, reflections) is a redesign of assessment around AI (P35).
units.anchor: Consider process-focused assignments and assessing intermediate milestones towards a final product

units.why: 'all detection tools are highly fallible' and faculty should 'be very cautious with accusations'; detectors are unreliable, so P39.
units.anchor: all detection tools are highly fallible, both with respect to false positives and false negatives

units.why: 'Apply enforcement policies uniformly to minimize bias' is a fairness requirement for enforcement; no type covers uniform enforcement (P64 is the student's right to respond; P36 is classification of misconduct).
units.anchor: Apply enforcement policies uniformly to minimize bias
units.uncovered_note: Apply enforcement of AI policies uniformly across students to minimize bias.

units.why: 'digitally savvy [students] are more likely to evade detection, and those who are less knowledgeable are more likely to end up in the dragnet' names an equity/bias harm of enforcement, so P53.
units.anchor: those who are less knowledgeable are more likely to end up in the dragnet

units.why: 'Focus on teaching students how to ethically and thoughtfully engage with GenAI, rather than only punishing misuse' makes teaching AI use an instructor aim; closest is P44 (courses teach AI use).
units.anchor: Focus on teaching students how to ethically and thoughtfully engage with GenAI

units.why: 'Consider issues of equity, access, and security when promoting GenAI usage' is the equity/access consideration (P51), addressed to faculty.
units.anchor: Consider issues of equity, access, and security when promoting GenAI usage in your courses

units.why: 'create assignments on the TerrierGPT platform, to which all BU students and faculty have free access' recommends the university-provided tool (P17); P51 not chosen since the main point is the sanctioned platform.
units.anchor: create assignments on the TerrierGPT platform
units.frag_start: If at all possible, create assignments
units.frag_end: not approved for use with restricted use data

units.why: TerrierGPT provides 'a high level of data security, up through confidential data' but 'is not approved for use with restricted use data'; data-protection facts about the vetted tool (P50).
units.anchor: high level of data security, up through confidential data
units.frag_start: This has the additional benefit of

units.why: 'For policies on GenAI use in broader academic and research contexts, please refer to' the faculty and staff guidelines defers research-context rules to another document (P62).
units.anchor: For policies on GenAI use in broader academic and research contexts, please refer to

units.why: 'We invite your feedback' signals the guidance is open to input and revision (P54).
units.anchor: We invite your feedback

documents.title: CDS Generative AI Assistance (GAIA) Policy
documents.summary: The CDS GAIA policy, drafted by students and adopted by CDS faculty in 2023, embraces AI tools with limits. Students credit AI, attach an appendix of the exchange, and use no AI in in-class exams or unpermitted assignments. Instructors grade declared AI use against a lower baseline and may impose stricter rules.
documents.stance_why: The policy 'adopts a few commonsense limitations on an otherwise embracing approach to AI tools' and requires credit and an appendix, so AI is allowed with conditions; instructors 'are free' to be stricter but the unit-wide default is permissive, so permit.

units.why: The policy 'adopts a few commonsense limitations on an otherwise embracing approach to AI tools', i.e. AI use is welcomed by default with limits (P02).
units.anchor: a few commonsense limitations on an otherwise embracing approach to AI tools

units.why: 'Students should learn how to use AI text generators ... to enhance rather than damage their developing abilities' presents learning to use AI well as the goal (P44).
units.anchor: Students should learn how to use AI text generators and other AI-based assistive resources

units.why: 'Instructors should ensure fair grading for both those who do and do not use AI tools' is a grading-design duty around AI (P35).
units.anchor: should ensure fair grading for both those who do and do not use AI tools

units.why: The policy 'stresses transparency, fairness, and honoring relevant stakeholders' and lists them; a statement of purpose and principles (P56).
units.anchor: stresses transparency, fairness, and honoring relevant stakeholders
units.frag_end: colleagues who lack privileged access to valuable resources

units.why: 'Students shall give credit to AI tools whenever used, even if only to generate ideas' is a disclosure/attribution duty for any use (P24).
units.anchor: Give credit to AI tools whenever used, even if only to generate ideas

units.why: The appendix must show 'the entire exchange, highlighting the most relevant sections'; students keep and submit the full transcript (P26).
units.anchor: add an appendix showing (a) the entire exchange, highlighting the most relevant sections
units.frag_start: When using AI tools on assignments

units.why: The appendix must give 'a description of precisely which AI tools were used (e.g. ChatGPT private subscription version or DALL-E free version)'; naming the tool/version is P25.
units.anchor: a description of precisely which AI tools were used

units.why: The appendix must include 'an explanation of how the AI tools were used' (generate ideas, turns of phrase, long stretches of text), a reflection on use (P26).
units.anchor: an explanation of how the AI tools were used

units.why: The appendix must include 'an account of why AI tools were used' (save time, writer's block, stress), a reflection on motive (P26).
units.anchor: an account of why AI tools were used

units.why: Students shall 'Not use AI tools during in-class examinations'; a ban on AI in in-class assessment (P22).
units.anchor: Not use AI tools during in-class examinations

units.why: 'or assignments, unless explicitly permitted and instructed' sets a fallback: for assignments AI is barred unless the instructor explicitly permits it (P06); the same sentence's exam ban is coded separately as P22.
units.anchor: or assignments, unless explicitly permitted and instructed
units.frag_start: Not use AI tools during in-class

units.why: Students shall 'Employ AI detection tools and originality checks prior to submission' to avoid being mistakenly flagged; students self-check with detectors, which fits no type (P40 is staff use of detectors to identify misuse).
units.anchor: Employ AI detection tools and originality checks prior to submission
units.frag_start: Employ AI detection tools and originality
units.uncovered_note: Students must run AI detection tools and originality checks on their own work before submitting.

units.why: 'Use AI tools wisely and intelligently, aiming to deepen understanding of subject matter and to support learning' encourages AI as a support for understanding (P12 tutor use) rather than for producing work.
units.anchor: Use AI tools wisely and intelligently, aiming to deepen understanding of subject matter
units.frag_start: Use AI tools wisely and intelligently

units.why: Instructors shall 'Seek to understand how AI tools work, including their strengths and weaknesses'; instructor learning about AI before teaching with it (P63).
units.anchor: Seek to understand how AI tools work, including their strengths and weaknesses

units.why: 'Treat work by students who declare no use of AI tools as the baseline for grading' sets a grading baseline tied to declared AI use, explicitly a redesign of grading around AI (P35).
units.anchor: work by students who declare no use of AI tools as the baseline for grading

units.why: 'Use a lower baseline for students who declare use of AI tools, depending on how extensive the usage' means declared use is graded lower; coded P35 (explicit baselines for declared use) though P28 (disclosed use still penalized) also fits.
units.anchor: Use a lower baseline for students who declare use of AI tools
units.frag_start: Use a lower baseline for students

units.why: Instructors shall 'Employ AI detection tools to evaluate the degree to which AI tools have likely been employed'; staff use of detectors to identify AI use (P40), in tension with P39.
units.anchor: AI detection tools to evaluate the degree to which AI tools have likely been employed
units.frag_start: Employ AI detection tools to evaluate

units.why: 'Impose a significant penalty for low-energy or unreflective reuse ... and assigning zero points for merely reproducing the output' states concrete penalties in advance (P37).
units.anchor: assigning zero points for merely reproducing the output from AI tools
units.frag_start: Impose a significant penalty for low-energy

units.why: 'This policy depends on goodwill, a sense of fairness, and honorable character' states the principle the policy rests on rather than a rule (P56).
units.anchor: This policy depends on goodwill, a sense of fairness, and honorable character

units.why: 'Some instructors may prefer stronger restrictions ... and they are free to impose them' lets each instructor set stricter rules (P04) provided grading stays transparent and fair.
units.anchor: free to impose them so long as care is taken to maintain transparency and fairness

units.why: The policy 'takes account of the existence of subscription versions of AI tools, which are not affordable for some students'; an equity/access concern (P51), with revision noted.
units.anchor: subscription versions of AI tools, which are not affordable for some students
units.frag_start: This policy takes account of the

units.why: 'This policy may be revised in light of other policies and novel technological developments' marks the policy as provisional (P54).
units.anchor: This policy may be revised in light of other policies and novel technological developments

units.why: The CDS committee 'recommended it for adoption by CDS, noting that instructors may adjust it as needed' lets instructors adapt the policy to course outcomes (P04).
units.anchor: instructors may adjust it as needed in support of the learning outcomes in their courses
units.frag_start: This policy was further discussed and

units.why: The policy covers tools that 'do not adhere to standards ... with respect to appropriation of others work and proper attribution' and 'should not be construed as endorsing this practice'; an ethical caveat about AI tools (P53).
units.anchor: The policy should not be construed as endorsing this practice

notes: Course layer deferred in collect file. Two UNCOVERED units: uniform enforcement (AIDA) and students self-running AI detectors (GAIA). GAIA lower-baseline unit could also be P28.
